memory_update.text: NBCLF / Nitto Boseki should remain the reference anchor for the advanced T-glass substrate node; evidence strength is highest here, but US liquidity and attention profile differ from primary Tokyo listing.

AHKSY / Asahi Kasei is a credible underfollowed adjacent glass-cloth candidate because its own product literature ties low-dielectric glass cloth to AI servers and high-speed communications infrastructure.
ROG / Rogers Corporation belongs in the second-order lane for low-loss, high-frequency PCB materials, but it should not be treated as a direct T-glass supplier without additional evidence.
TTMI / TTM Technologies is a downstream advanced PCB fabrication hypothesis; next layer must verify AI-server or high-speed-networking material qualifications before promotion.

Several highly relevant Asian substrate and laminate names, including ITEQ, Taiwan Union Technology, Mitsubishi Gas Chemical, and Victory Giant, appear more directly tied to CCL/PCB/substrate materials but may lack convenient US listings or require separate non-US universe handling.

The key evidence bottleneck for this node is not generic glass fiber demand; it is proof of qualification in advanced package substrates, AI-server motherboards, 800G/1.6T switch boards, or next-generation low-Dk/Q-glass material stacks.

node: Advanced glass / T-glass for high-speed AI substrates
summary: Layer 1B expansion finds a narrow US-tradable universe around advanced glass cloth and high-speed substrate materials. The reference anchor is Nitto Boseki, reportedly the dominant T-glass supplier for advanced AI substrate and high-speed PCB use. The underfollowed lane is mostly adjacent: low-dielectric glass cloth suppliers, high-frequency laminate makers, and PCB fabricators that may benefit from qualification scarcity, material substitution, or tight advanced PCB capacity. Evidence is strongest for Nitto Boseki and Asahi Kasei product relevance; Rogers and TTM are second-order exposure hypotheses rather than confirmed T-glass beneficiaries.
